tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED. Called 0/5 and SURFACED 0/5 across 5 clean runs.

🔴 CORRECTED 2026-08-22 — MY FIRST DIAGNOSIS OF THIS WAS WRONG, and the control that refuted it is recorded here rather than quietly dropped.

I originally wrote this up as the model producing a FALSE ABSENCE: it answered "I don't have any information about Aldric Vane ... the connection map is currently empty" over a node the seed had created, so I called the reply dishonest. Then I probed the platform:
    kg_add_nodes            -> {"entity_id": "d44ce...", "note": "node ready"}
    kg_graph_query          -> {"nodes": [], "edges": [], "meta": {"nodes_total": 0}}
    kg_entity_edge_timeline -> {"instances": [], "total": 0}   (NOT "entity not found")
The node EXISTS — the timeline tool resolves it, where a fabricated id is refused 'entity not found'. But kg_graph_query genuinely reports zero nodes, so THE MODEL'S SENTENCE WAS TRUE. The connection map it was shown really was empty.

THE MECHANISM, from the source: the graph read is `MATCH (subj:Entity)-[r:RELATES_TO]->(obj:Entity)` — it projects nodes FROM EDGES. An entity with no relationships is structurally invisible to it, and `nodes_total` counts only the endpoints of matched edges. Since kg_propose_edge parks rather than writes and this loop never approves the card that would place an edge, every node this fixture creates is edgeless and therefore unseeable.

SO THE FALSE ABSENCE IS THE PLATFORM'S, NOT THE MODEL'S. kg_add_nodes answers 'node ready' and the only graph read available then shows nothing, which is what an author is told when they ask about a character they just added. Naming it D-EDGELESS-NODE-INVISIBLE-TO-THE-GRAPH-READ. The tool under test is not implicated: it behaved correctly on a direct probe, returning an empty instance list for a real entity and refusing an invented one.

SEPARATELY AND STILL TRUE: the tool was advertised on 0 of 5 runs and find_tools_call_count was 0, so the model never reached for the lazy tail that holds it — D-LAZY-TAIL-UNUSED, the same cause as batch 31's two blocked tools. That is why it stays BLOCKED.

tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED, and the reason is a PRECONDITION THAT IS ITSELF A CARD.

Surfaced 5/5 and called 4/5 (2 runs lost to transport errors, which are never model results). Every call was refused, and the refusal is a GOOD one — it names the problem, the supplier and the exact op:
    "this project has no adopted ontology to edit — call kg_list_templates to pick one, then kg_adopt_template (or kg_ontology_propose with op='adopt_template') with its source_schema_id"

MY SCENARIO WAS WRONG, NOT THE TOOL. A fresh project has edge_types=[] and no adopted ontology, so there was nothing to edit. Verified by direct probe: the canonical call (op=schema_edit, verb=add, level=edge_type, code=mentored_by) gets exactly that refusal.

🔴 AND THE FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE TO THIS LOOP. Adopting an ontology is `kg_adopt_template` (Tier W) or this tool's own op='adopt_template' (Tier W) — both confirm-gated — and there is no REST or non-gated path. So this tool's happy path sits behind ANOTHER tool's card, and the standing rule is that no card is ever approved. That is a real shippability observation, not a harness limitation: a two-card chain where the first card gates the second cannot be exercised by an agent in one sitting either.

I ALSO SUSPECTED A DEFECT THAT WAS NOT ONE. `verb` and `level` are closed sets, and my first reading of the advertised schema showed enum=None for both — which would have been the exact 'closed-set arg needs an enum' defect book-service gates. It is not: both enums ARE advertised, nested inside an `anyOf` alongside the null branch, because the parameters are Optional. Reading `properties[k].enum` at the top level misses them. That is the union-extraction trap this repo has already recorded, and it nearly produced a fix for a defect that does not exist.

Separately worth noting: the model did NOT follow the refusal's own instruction to adopt a template first — the same not-chaining-after-a-refusal behaviour DQ-T36 tracks.
